quest.title: Where Ancient Stars Align
quest.description: The meteorites that have rained down were once, in fact, part of someone's constellation. Why did this ancient array of stars fall from the sky? What goal were their extinguished flames chasing? Armed with the courage to face the answers, you march onward.
quest.rewards_formatted: Fragile Resin x1, Primogem x60, Mora x30000

talks.objective: Ask Mona about the progress of her scrying

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Is Fischl waiting for us?

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: The time has finally come. Though it brings mein Fräulein no joy to do so, there is something she must announce to the assembled populous.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: My loyal servants, one must bid you adieu till such time as I beckon you once more. Though we have faced many trials and tribulations together, you have all shown commendable courage in the course of duty. I feel a breeze now blows upon this place... and I feel that it blows in your honor.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whaaaat? You're just gonna bail on us!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Fischl, are you leaving?

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: With the arrival of this giant meteorite, many more people have succumbed to the slumber. Strong as the soldiers may be, they are struggling to cope, and there is demand for volunteers everywhere we turn.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Mein Fräulein and I shall tend to the victims on the soldiers' behalf. The rest of this investigation we place in your capable hands.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: #...Goodbye, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: You are a good listener. ...I enjoy chatting with you.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: To be honest, most of the other adventurers in the Guild only ever talk to me when they wanna hear Oz's reconnaissance reports...

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: This little journey we had... it was a great adventure. I'm just sorry that it has to end so abruptly...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You're talking a little weirder than you normally do...

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: (Yikes!!! What am I doing? I totally broke form...)

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: What mein Fräulein means to say, is... is... is that the mystical mysteries that vex and perplex are bound to be effortlessly extinguished by the advent of your commendable courage and wondrous wisdom.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... And now Oz's translation is the one that sounds all kooky.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Ahem... Mein Fräulein simply wishes to say that she has every confidence that you will arrive at the truth of this matter.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Ahem! Most indeed... My dear attendants, I hereby charge the Ritter der Verurteilung with leading you out from the darkness, back into the realm of light.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Who are you calling your "attendant..."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you Oz, and thank you Fischl.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: We will meet again. Once this matter is concluded, I propose that we all get a drink together.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Well, now we're two people short.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: But let's not get hung up about that. The good news is, I've found something else out.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I shaved some dust off the meteorite and used it to do another reading. It was actually really effective!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: These rocks have been around for hundreds, maybe even thousands of years. Leonard must have lived a very long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: The meteorites carry his will, and can pass it on to others. In other words, centuries on from Leonard's life, and the strength of his will has not diminished one bit.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: A guy from the distant past with a burning ambition to scale the highest mountain... I'd be willing to bet that he was an adventurer, just like you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: An adventurer? That does explain his obsession with mountain climbing!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Our approach so far has been too passive, and time has been against us every step of the way. We need to change our strategy, and we need to attack this problem at its source.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon agrees! From now on, we need to put Leonard at the center of everything we do.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Yes... Because if the meteorites carry Leonard's will with them, then it's precisely as Fischl said: the rocks are, in a sense, a curse...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I'm a little incredulous, but it turns out her blind guess was actually spot on... Ugh, no, I'm a respectable astrologist, and I shouldn't stoop to that kind of criticism.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Anyway. All we need to do now is remove the curse.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Come on Paimon, let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okie-dokie!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Since we've got a historical adventurer on our hands, Paimon thinks we should pay a visit to the <color=#00E1FFFF>Adventurers' Guild</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Our records show that there have been many adventurers by that name over the years, it is impossible to know which one you refer to.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: However, I do recall that there is a book in the library authored by someone called Leonard. Perhaps you should take a look?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: However, I do recall that there is a book in the <color=#00E1FFFF>library</color> authored by someone called Leonard. Perhaps you should take a look?

talks.objective: Search for clues in the Mondstadt Library

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Author, Leonard... Where are you, Leonard... Aha! Gotcha!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The index says that Leonard's book should be in the <color=#00E1FFFF>north-west corner</color> on the <color=#00E1FFFF>first floor</color> of the library.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: North-west corner... Should be right over there.

talks.objective: Check the index in front of Lisa's desk
Look for the book Leonard authored

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Found it! "Of Mountains and Seas," A Guide for Adventurers, written by Leonard!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But the words have faded and there are even pages missing... Paimon's got no hope of reading this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Darn... Maybe we're just wasting our time on this one?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't give up. Let's see what Mona says.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right, yeah! Mona! She might have a better idea.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look what we found, Leonard wrote a book!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Ooh, let me see!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's quite incoherent as there is lots missing.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Hm! I could have predicted as much...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Your average astrologist would definitely give up at this point.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: But I am Mona, progenitor of the future of astrology. Nothing can stand in my way.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I simply need to deduce the missing portions with my astrolabe, write them in, and then decipher the text...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Phew! Finished at last...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what does it say?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Just as I thought, Leonard was an adventurer who lived two thousand years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: His lifelong dream was to reach the summit of a mountain called Pilos Peak.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Two thousand years? So the constellation that caused the meteorites is from two thousand years ago!?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Somehow, for some reason, this constellation was summoned down from the sky. I suspect that the Fatui have something to do with that part.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks so too. Whenever something shady happens, you can bet the Fatui are involved.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: The meteorites harbor elemental energy, which radiates out and lulls people to sleep by some means akin to hypnosis.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: And if I'm guessing correctly, there should be some sort of core meteorite among the bunch, within which is a crystal that harbors Leonard's spirit.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How will we find it?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Well, if I were Leonard, I would want to make sure the core lands right on the snowy summit that I never made it to while I was alive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the core should be at the top of Pilos Peak? Where is that? Paimon's never heard of it before.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: It's the first I'd heard of it too, so I compared the map from the book against the current topography of Mondstadt. Apparently, Pilos Peak no longer exists.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you trying to say that the tallest mountain Paimon's never heard of just... disappeared!?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I once read somewhere that the Anemo Archon, Barbatos, once used his divine power to mobilize the winds and blow the ice and snow from the face of the earth. The whole landscape of Mondstadt was changed in the process.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: The mountains of that age were replaced by the vast stretch of ocean we see today. Still, a mountain that high? Drop it into the ocean and it'll still leave a trace.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: The summit still reaches just above the water's surface. So, the place known as Pilos Peak in Leonard's day is today known...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: ...as <color=#00E1FFFF>"Musk Reef."</color>

talks.objective: Go to Musk Reef as the book indicates

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Ho? So this is Pilos Peak? Not much to show for itself now, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like someone beat us here... Is this, like, a popular tourist spot, or...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! It's you!

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Ugh... Huh? You again?

choices.text: How did you find this place?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Look at the state he's in... Was he in that dream just now?

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: He managed to extricate himself from the dream on his own strength? How is that possible?

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: Hah! Just because you are powerless to do something does not mean that I am.

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: You're too late, anyway. I've finished my research.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We knew it! This was all a dirty trick by the Fatui!

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: Save it. No more fun and games for me today. I'll come for you when I'm good and ready.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait! What are you trying to achieve?

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: You entered the dream they've all been having, didn't you? How much do you know about Leonard?

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: Leonard? Who's Leonard? ...Ugh, whatever! I have bigger fish to fry!

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: I've discovered something far more important... and far more terrifying.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What is it?

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: The stars, the sky... It's all a gigantic hoax. A lie.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: The stars are a lie? What are you talking about?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is this some kind of astrological debate between you and Mona? Because if so, surely you can come up with a better argument than "The stars are a lie."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seriously, who's gonna fall for that one when you can just lift your head up at night and see them up there, twinkling away?

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: Hah... Hahahahaha! Oh, you are so naive, it kills me!

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: Still... Can't really blame you. After all, I used to believe the same thing myself — up until a few moments ago, that is...

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: A few moments ago? You mean...

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: Look — I really don't have the time to do this right now.

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: What was the Jester thinking? He must have had some inkling of what we might discover on this mission... Would it really have been so difficult to give me a little forewarning? Hmph, or maybe he just wanted to give me a fright...

response.speaker: The Balladeer
response.text: Time for me to go out and find the truth. So long, suckers!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you fought so fiercely!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Told you! That's what happens when you disrespect me!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mona, you are a force to be reckoned with.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: You bet I am! Paimon, you agree too, right? Did I show those Fatui who's boss or what?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure did! Without you here, those guys would have caused us a whole lot more trouble!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: See! How do you like that, Harbinger! Scumbag...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: He seemed genuinely shaken, though. I don't think he was lying. I was always taught to talk about the "false sky" during astrological readings... Could there be more to such phrases than I have been led to believe?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: ...Ahem. I digress. Come on, let's finish the job we came to do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The <color=#00E1FFFF>core</color> has gotta be round here somewhere!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, this must be the core... It looks totally different from all the other meteorites! It's way more... shiny.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: This stone harbors an unbelievable amount of elemental energy, and human desire. It's the core alright.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Should we... destroy it?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Yes. Otherwise, the victims will never wake up... This core is the root cause of everything that has happened.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Do it, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Wow. Well, that was unexpected...

choices.text: A climber, determined to reach the highest peak.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Who would have thought that human will can survive in the skies for millennia on end...

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Astrology really is an incredible thing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...What makes you say that?

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: The ability to communicate with the stars can give you access to all the secrets from throughout human history... Though of course, very few astrologists ever reach that level.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Mona, thank you ever so much for all of your assistance.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Uh... What's with the formal tone all of a sudden?

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: And speaking of formal tone... What is the deal with that girl, Fischl? She's a curious one.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks so, too! She's soooo... How to put this...

choices.text: She's full of weird and wonderful thoughts.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... Although, if you think about it... Seems she was right all along.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is she one of these people who uses the wrong method but still gets the right answer?

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: You may well be right.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even so, Paimon thinks that the most surprising thing of all was how Pilos Peak turned into a teeny-tiny little island!

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: A mountain of yesteryear now sits as an island in the sea. Almost anyone from Mondstadt could reach it now, just by jumping in a boat.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In other words, everyone can climb Pilos Peak now.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Everyone can stand on top of the mountain.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: D'you think Leonard would be happy about it? The situation with Pilos Peak might be a bit of a shock... but now, with the help of the Anemo Archon, the people of Mondstadt are able to glide.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: With wings, people can travel further and higher than ever before, and explore new and unknown places.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Leonard, is your wish now fulfilled?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The victims should finally start waking up now that we've dealt with the core.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And we have finally finished our commission from the Adventurers' Guild!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I wish everyone a speedy recovery.

choices.text: Determination so strong, he wished to pass it on to others.
